blocking_findings.description: Valid JSON arrays are transformed into tuples before JsonValue validation. PlanInput and SelectionRecord inherit CheckedValue, whose recursive unpack converts every list into a tuple, including lists nested inside settings, controlled_factors and random_draw. JsonValue's JSON variants do not include tuples. Consequently ordinary inputs such as settings={"schedule":[1,2]} or random_draw={"indices":[0,1]} fail instead of being retained. An independent execution of the actual unpack function confirmed this transformation; full Pydantic validation could not be executed in this environment. Existing tests use only scalar-valued objects and null.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Preserve JSON array representation while retaining copied-model revalidation. Add positive cases for nested arrays in all three JSON-valued fields through construction, repository admission, read-back and CLI JSON input, with explicit expected values.

blocking_findings.description: Binding through a byte-identical alias does not consistently reuse the established lineage's origin. For example, bind a PLANNED clip, register the same bytes without --plan in another dataset, then bind that FOUND alias. The helper reuses the prior binding ID, media and registration, but computes origin=FOUND from the alias. Existing admission correctly rejects this successor because the prior origin was GENERATED. The reverse direction also fails. Thus a valid alias cannot perform the promised later binding while preserving the original anchors. The alias test covers only matching FOUND origins.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Resolve existing lineage anchors and their retained origin context before assembling a successor. Preserve the established binding origin when operating through an alias, keep context validation consistent, and test both cross-origin alias directions without weakening nonpromotion or origin immutability.

claims_for_research.claim: Pydantic model_copy(update=...) does not validate supplied update values; verify applicability to the locked Pydantic 2.13.5 version.
SQLite permits one simultaneous write transaction, and BEGIN IMMEDIATE requests that transaction immediately and can fail with SQLITE_BUSY.
SQLite triggers using RAISE(ABORT, message) terminate UPDATE or DELETE statements with a constraint error.
Python 3.12 hashlib guarantees a sha256 constructor and hexadecimal digest output.
RFC 8785 sorts object property names by UTF-16 code units and encodes the resulting serialization as UTF-8.
The locked Pydantic JsonValue validator rejects tuples produced by CheckedValue.unpack instead of accepting them as JSON arrays; confirm this dependency behavior underlying L04-R1-F01.
